# Behavioral Design Specification: SPI Host FSM

## 1. Purpose

This module is the transaction controller for a SPI host. It accepts command-segment descriptors, generates the SPI clock and chip-select timing, controls data-line direction, and coordinates the loading, shifting, sampling, and unloading of data in the SPI datapath.

The module supports:

- Multiple chip-select lines, parameterized at instantiation.
- Standard, Dual, and Quad SPI speed modes.
- Transmit-only, receive-only, bidirectional, and dummy segments.
- Programmable clock polarity, clock phase, clock divider, and chip-select timing.
- Back-to-back segments with chip-select stay-active operation.
- Stall handling when the SPI datapath or FIFO is not ready to proceed.

## 2. Reset and Initialization

### 2.1 System Reset

On system reset:

- The module shall enter an idle state.
- All chip-select outputs shall be deasserted.
- The SPI clock output shall be at its idle level.
- All data output-enable outputs shall be deasserted.
- The module shall not accept commands.
- The active status output shall be low.

### 2.2 Enable and Disable

The module shall only accept and process commands when enabled.

- When disabled, the module shall not accept new commands.
- If disabled during an active transaction, the module shall hold all outputs stable and shall not advance the transaction.
- When re-enabled, the module shall resume from the point at which it was stopped.

### 2.3 Software Reset

A software reset input shall take precedence over normal operation.

When software reset is asserted, the module shall:

- Return to its idle state.
- Clear all byte, bit, and timing progress counters.
- Deassert all chip-select outputs.
- Place the SPI clock at its configured idle level.
- Deassert all data output enables.
- Stop accepting commands until software reset is deasserted.

Software reset shall not change the stored device configuration. After release, the module shall use the configuration that was active before the reset.

## 3. Command and Configuration Handling

### 3.1 Command Segment Descriptor

The module accepts one command segment at a time. Each segment descriptor contains:

- The target chip-select index.
- Device configuration:
  - Clock polarity.
  - Clock phase.
  - Clock divider value.
  - Chip-select lead, trail, and idle timing values.
  - Full-cycle sampling enable.
- Segment execution fields:
  - Data direction (transmit, receive, bidirectional, or dummy).
  - Speed mode (Standard, Dual, or Quad).
  - Segment length.
  - Chip-select stay-active flag.

### 3.2 Command Acceptance

A command segment shall be accepted only when:

- The module is enabled.
- The command-valid input is asserted.
- The command-ready output is asserted.
- The module is not stalled.

The module shall assert command-ready when it is able to accept a new segment. Command-ready shall be suppressed during stall conditions.

The module shall accept a new segment:

- From the normal idle state.
- From the idle-with-chip-select-active state, if the new segment targets the same chip-select line and is intended to continue the current transaction.
- At the end of a stay-active segment, if the next segment is already pending.

If a pending command targets a different chip-select while the current chip select is held active, the module shall not accept the command immediately. It shall first terminate the current transaction, perform the required trail and idle timing, and then accept the new command.

### 3.3 Configuration Changes

The module shall only apply a change to device configuration while all chip-select lines are inactive.

If the incoming segment specifies configuration options that differ from the currently active configuration, the module shall:

1. Complete the idle timing required by the previous configuration.
2. Switch to the new configuration.
3. Wait for the idle timing required by the new configuration.
4. Only then assert the new chip select and start the segment.

This extra idle time shall also be inserted when changing between different chip-select targets with different configuration options.

## 4. SPI Clock Generation

### 4.1 Clock Polarity

The SPI clock output shall be generated according to the configured clock polarity:

- CPOL = 0: idle level low, active pulses high.
- CPOL = 1: idle level high, active pulses low.

The clock shall remain at the idle level outside active data/dummy clocking periods, including lead, trail, idle, configuration-switch, and chip-select-active idle states.

### 4.2 Clock Divider

The SPI clock frequency shall be controlled by the clock divider value.

The SPI clock shall have a period of:

`2 × (CLKDIV + 1)` system clock cycles.

This divided half-period shall also define the timing granularity for chip-select lead, trail, and idle delays.

### 4.3 Clock Output During Active Segments

During an active segment, the SPI clock shall toggle continuously at the configured rate until the segment length has been completed.

The module shall not produce spurious clock pulses while entering or leaving the active clocking portion of a transaction.

## 5. Chip-Select and Transaction Timing

### 5.1 Normal Single-Segment Transaction

For a normal segment where the chip-select stay-active flag is clear, the module shall perform the following sequence:

1. Assert the selected chip-select output low.
2. Wait for the configured lead delay.
3. Generate SPI clock pulses for the segment.
4. After the last required clock edge, wait for the configured trail delay while the selected chip-select is still asserted.
5. Deassert all chip-select outputs high.
6. Wait for the configured idle delay.
7. Return to the idle state and indicate ready to accept a new command.

All chip-select outputs except the selected one shall remain deasserted throughout the transaction.

### 5.2 Lead, Trail, and Idle Delays

The minimum delays shall be:

- Lead delay: `CSNLEAD + 1` half SPI clock periods.
- Trail delay: `CSNTRAIL + 1` half SPI clock periods.
- Idle delay: `CSNIDLE + 1` half SPI clock periods.

These delays shall be measured between:

- Chip-select assertion and the first active edge of the SPI clock.
- The last active edge of the SPI clock and chip-select deassertion.
- Chip-select deassertion and the next chip-select assertion.

### 5.3 Chip-Select Stay-Active Operation

When the chip-select stay-active flag is set, the module shall hold the selected chip-select asserted after the last clock edge of the segment instead of deasserting it.

If the next segment is already available and targets the same chip-select line, the module shall begin the next segment without inserting lead, trail, or idle delays.

If the next segment is not yet available, the module shall enter a chip-select-active idle state. In this state:

- The selected chip-select remains asserted.
- The SPI clock remains at its idle level.
- The active status output shall be low.
- The module shall be ready to accept a continuation segment for the same chip-select.

When a continuation segment arrives, clocking shall resume immediately from the appropriate clock phase.

### 5.4 Switching Chip-Select Targets

If a new segment targets a different chip-select line, the module shall terminate the current transaction even if the stay-active flag is set.

The sequence shall be:

1. Complete the current segment.
2. Wait for the trail delay using the old device configuration.
3. Deassert all chip-select outputs.
4. Wait for the idle delay using the old device configuration.
5. If required, wait for the additional configuration-switch idle delay using the new device configuration.
6. Assert the new chip-select output.
7. Wait for the lead delay.
8. Begin the new segment.

## 6. Data Path Control

### 6.1 Segment Direction

The module shall interpret the segment direction as follows:

- **Transmit-only**: Bytes shall be loaded from the transmit data source into the SPI datapath. The configured data outputs shall be enabled.
- **Receive-only**: Bytes shall be captured from the SPI data lines and transferred to the receive data sink. The data outputs shall be disabled.
- **Bidirectional**: Simultaneous transmit and receive shall occur. This mode is only supported in Standard SPI speed.
- **Dummy**: The SPI clock shall run for the specified number of clock cycles, but no data shall be transmitted or received. Data outputs shall be disabled.

### 6.2 Segment Length

For data segments, the segment length shall be interpreted as a number of bytes.

For dummy segments, the segment length shall be interpreted as a number of SPI clock cycles.

### 6.3 Speed Mode and Data Width

The module shall select the number of serial data lines used per clock cycle based on the speed mode:

- **Standard**: 1 bit per SPI clock cycle; 8 SPI clock cycles per byte.
- **Dual**: 2 bits per SPI clock cycle; 4 SPI clock cycles per byte.
- **Quad**: 4 bits per SPI clock cycle; 2 SPI clock cycles per byte.

The module shall output the current speed mode to the datapath so that shifting and sampling widths are selected correctly.

### 6.4 Data Output Enables

The module shall control the data output-enable outputs according to the current segment and chip-select state.

When all chip-select outputs are deasserted, all data output enables shall be deasserted.

When a chip select is asserted and the segment is transmitting data:

- Standard mode shall drive only the first data line.
- Dual mode shall drive the first two data lines.
- Quad mode shall drive all four data lines.

When a segment is receive-only or dummy, all data output enables shall be deasserted.

### 6.5 Clock Phase and Data Timing

The module shall time its datapath control pulses so that the selected clock phase is satisfied:

- With CPHA = 0, output data shall be presented when the chip select asserts, and shall change on the appropriate non-sampling edge of the SPI clock. Input data shall be captured on the sampling edge.
- With CPHA = 1, output data shall change on the leading edge of the SPI clock, and input data shall be captured on the trailing edge.

The module shall generate:

- A load pulse when a new transmit byte is to be inserted into the datapath.
- Shift pulses to advance the datapath by the correct number of bits for the current speed mode.
- Sample pulses to capture incoming data at the correct sampling point.
- A read pulse when a complete received byte is available to be transferred to the receive data sink.

### 6.6 Full-Cycle Sampling

When full-cycle sampling is enabled, the module shall adjust the sampling point so that incoming data is captured one full SPI clock period after the point at which the remote device drives the data.

Full-cycle mode shall not affect the SPI clock output, chip-select timing, or output data timing.

The module shall output an indication of full-cycle mode to the datapath so that the datapath can apply the correct sampling behavior.

### 6.7 Last-Byte Indications

When the module issues a load pulse for the final byte of a transmit or bidirectional segment, it shall also assert the last-write indication together with that load pulse.

When the module issues a read pulse for the final byte of a receive or bidirectional segment, it shall also assert the last-read indication together with that read pulse.

These indications shall only be asserted when the corresponding data transfer is actually taking place.

## 7. Stall and Flow Control

### 7.1 Transmit Stall

The module shall detect a transmit stall when it is ready to load a new byte into the datapath but the transmit data source is not ready.

During a transmit stall, the module shall:

- Assert the transmit-stall status output.
- Suppress the load pulse.
- Hold all internal progress.
- Hold the SPI clock and chip-select outputs stable.
- Stop accepting new commands.

### 7.2 Receive Stall

The module shall detect a receive stall when it has completed a received byte but the receive data sink is not ready to accept it.

During a receive stall, the module shall:

- Assert the receive-stall status output.
- Suppress the read pulse.
- Hold all internal progress.
- Hold the SPI clock and chip-select outputs stable.
- Stop accepting new commands.

### 7.3 Global Stall Effect

Either stall condition shall halt the entire FSM.

While stalled:

- No state advancement shall occur.
- No counters shall be updated.
- No data-path control pulses shall be generated.
- No command shall be accepted.
- The SPI clock shall not toggle.
- Chip-select outputs shall remain unchanged.

When the stall condition clears, the module shall resume normal operation from the exact point at which it stalled.

## 8. Status Outputs

### 8.1 Active Status

The active status output shall be asserted whenever the module is not in an idle state.

It shall be asserted during:

- Chip-select lead timing.
- Active SPI clock generation.
- Chip-select trail timing.
- Inter-transaction idle timing.
- Configuration-switch idle timing.

It shall be deasserted when the module is waiting in a normal idle state or in a chip-select-active idle state.

### 8.2 Speed and Full-Cycle Indications

The module shall continuously output the speed mode and full-cycle sampling flag associated with the currently active segment.

These outputs shall change only at segment boundaries and shall remain stable while a segment is being processed.
